title: Distributed systems: partitioning, replication and fault tolerance

videos.script: Roda Livre keeps its rides in one database, on one machine. {{one-machine}} That is fine, until it is not. The data stops fitting. Or the machine stops, at six in the evening, with every bicycle out. {{why}} So the data is spread over several machines. And three things arrive that one machine never had. A network that loses messages. Clocks that disagree. And a machine that fails while the others carry on. {{three-things}} This lesson is about the answers. Partitioning splits the data, so each machine holds a part. {{partitioning}} Replication copies each part, so it survives losing a machine. {{replication}} And fault tolerance is what you do when a reply never comes. {{fault-tolerance}} You will see each one happen, in short programs on your own machine. Ten thousand rides on four partitions, with one station far too busy. {{skew}} A copy that answers with what was true a second ago. {{stale}} And a payment tried three times that charges once. {{retry}} You will not build a database here. You will learn what one is doing underneath, so that its strange days make sense. {{end}}
